question.text: Which statement about preference shares is correct?

answer.text: Preference shares are hybrid securities combining features of both equity and debt
Only convertible preference shares are hybrid
Only cumulative preference shares are hybrid
Preference shares are purely debt instruments with no equity features

explanation.text: The Logic: Preference shares are hybrid securities. They share equity features (dividend payments that may or may not be declared, no collateral backing the instrument) and debt features (a finite life and a stated dividend rate on the par value). They also carry preferential rights over equity for dividends and capital repayment. The Trap: Restricting the hybrid label to convertible or cumulative variants is wrong because all preference shares are hybrid by their basic features. They are not purely debt instruments either, since they lack the collateral and senior-claim protections of debt. Note: Stem reworded from "Which type of preference shares..." to "Which statement about preference shares is correct?" so the keyed full-statement option fits grammatically, and the role-specific pro-tip has been removed.
